entities.name: Andronikos II of Trebizond
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Andronikos II Megas Komnenos, or Andronicus II Grand Comnenus, was the Emperor of Trebizond from 1263 to 1266. Despite being the designated successor of his father Manuel I, Andronikos' tenure was short due to premature death from unrecorded causes. The major event of his reign was the definitive loss of Sinope to the Seljuk Turks under the regency of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman, also known as the Pervane, in the summer or fall of 1265. The capture of Sinope by the Turks gave them the best port on the Black Sea, allowing them to create a navy and compete with the Trapezuntines for influence in the Black Sea.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Andronikos II's loss of Sinope to the Seljuk Turks marked a significant regional shift in Black Sea politics, as it gave the Turks control over the best port on the sea and allowed them to create a navy. This event had lasting consequences for the region.
